## Report

When `review-plan` PASSES but the attestation write fails, it prints:

    plan review PASSED but the attestation could not be persisted: flock: could not acquire lock after 60s
    run `rebar sign-review <id>` to re-sign from the recorded review (no LLM re-run) — the claim gate needs the signature.

That guidance is sound only when the PASS **sidecar** persisted and only the signature
failed. When one contention episode takes BOTH, `sign-review` cannot recover and returns:

    {"ok": false, "signed": false, "verdict": "BLOCK",
     "reason": "the latest review was not a signable PASS (verdict=BLOCK) — run `rebar review-plan` to produce a fresh verdict"}

Observed twice while earning the attestation for bug royal-weariless-zebrafish; the payload
carried `"sidecar_emitted": false` both times. Each occurrence cost a full ~14-minute,
28-LLM-call review. Worse than losing the result: the recorded verdict silently remains the
PREVIOUS round's BLOCK, so the system retains a **stale contradicting** verdict rather than
no verdict, and the advertised recovery walks the reader into it.

## Premise verified in current `origin/main` (cc69cc1179)

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py`:

* `classify_plan_review_attestation(result)` — line **485** — is the single producer of the
  post-failure guidance. It already discriminates three cases on the *signature* dict:
  `plan_review_generation_changed` (line 505, `recovery_tool="review_plan"`),
  `_is_relation_read_failure` (line 526, `recovery_tool="review_plan"`), and a final
  catch-all (lines **544-556**, `recovery_tool="sign_review"`).
* That catch-all is reached for **any** non-material failure — including the lock timeout —
  and it **never inspects `sidecar_emitted`**, which is present on the very `result` dict it
  is handed (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:747` sets
  `verdict["sidecar_emitted"]`; the field is contracted in
  `src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verdict.schema.json:83`).

So the bug is exactly one missing discriminator on an existing, well-shaped decision
function. `sign-review`'s own refusal is correct and is not changed here.

## Direction

Add a fourth branch to `classify_plan_review_attestation`, ahead of the catch-all, taken when
the failure is a sign failure AND `result.get("sidecar_emitted")` is falsy: a new
`ATTESTATION_SIDECAR_LOST` cause with `recovery_tool="review_plan"`, whose message

1. does **not** name `sign-review`,
2. states that no PASS record persisted, so a fresh `rebar review-plan <id>` is required, and
3. warns that the recorded verdict is still the PREVIOUS round's and must not be read as
   current.

The existing `sidecar_emitted=True` path keeps the cheap no-LLM `sign-review` recovery
unchanged. `ATTESTATION_SIDECAR_LOST` joins the sibling constants at lines 412-425 and is
covered by the same `as_dict()` machine-branchable payload (line 457), so agents branch on
`cause`/`recovery_tool` without parsing English.

Scope note: this is a **classification + message** change only. No LLM behaviour, no sidecar
write path, no `sign-review` semantics, and no CLI exit code changes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failed-sign result with `sidecar_emitted=False` classifies as
      `cause=ATTESTATION_SIDECAR_LOST` with `recovery_tool="review_plan"`, and its message
      contains no `sign-review` string — verified by a unit test on
      `classify_plan_review_attestation`
- [ ] A failed-sign result with `sidecar_emitted=True` still classifies as
      `cause=ATTESTATION_SIGN_FAILED` with `recovery_tool="sign_review"` and still emits the
      no-LLM re-sign guidance — verified by a unit test
- [ ] The sidecar-lost message states that the recorded verdict is the previous round's and
      is not current — verified by a test asserting that text
- [ ] The `plan_review_generation_changed` and relation-read-failure branches are unchanged
      when `sidecar_emitted=False` (the new branch does not shadow them) — verified by a test
